extraction.name: 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU
extraction.description: A paper introducing training methods for CIFAR-10 that reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, including a derandomized horizontal flipping augmentation called alternating flip and released code at a GitHub repository.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper uses the CIFAR-10 dataset and describes loading the training and test data through torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10, saving them locally as train.pt and test.pt, and using the training set statistics to initialize the whitening convolution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 images and labels from torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10; the dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images divided into 50,000 training images and 10,000 validation/test images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images are converted to tensors, normalized with CIFAR-10 mean and standard deviation, optionally horizontally flipped, padded with reflection padding for translation augmentation, randomly cropped, and used to compute patch-whitening initialization from the first 5,000 normalized training images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The loader converts raw uint8 images to half precision tensors, permutes them to channels-first format, normalizes them, and applies augmentation; the first layer whitening initialization uses patches extracted from 5,000 training images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset labels are the CIFAR-10 class labels; the paper does not describe how the original annotations were created.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10, PyTorch, torch.compile, FFCV (for ImageNet experiments only), and the paper's custom alternating_flip implementation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The code is released as the airbench Python package and at the GitHub repository https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench; no explicit versioning, update schedule, maintainer policy, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that faster CIFAR-10 training can accelerate research, reduce experimental cost, and enable more computationally intensive studies by lowering the cost of training many networks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The method is designed for CIFAR-10 training speed under fixed hardware and performance constraints; the paper notes that some improvements may not generalize to scenarios where horizontal flipping is not beneficial, and that the approach is optimized for wall-clock time on an NVIDIA A100 rather than FLOP reduction.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, evaluation, and benchmarking on CIFAR-10; the released methods are intended for experiments where many networks are trained at once and for replicating or extending CIFAR-10 studies with fewer computational resources.
